doc.title: Onaje Allan Gumbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001

title: Arranging for Billy Taylor on the David Frost show
summary: Billy Taylor lets him write an arrangement for the Frost show; a chart error delays it, then it airs repeatedly.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Herbie Hancock. Now mind you he’s only like all of twenty something years old, but to me he was like this legend, and he’s still in his twenties. But I got to know him and really it was an incredible situation, but while I was in college, Billy Taylor, Dr. Billy Taylor, afforded me the opportunity to arrange — compose and arrange — some music for a show he was the musical director of at that time, that was David Frost. And I had gone to him and said I’d like to write something for the show. And he said well come back in August. So I thought it was like a W.C. Fields line — go away kid, you’re bothering me. So I came back and he said, “Well how soon can you write something?” And I was like oh damn, he really wants me to do it. So I wrote this arrangement, composed and arranged it, they copied it out professionally and everything. And I go back to school, and this is about the time we were at the house, in the senior year, I turn on David Frost every day, didn’t hear my song. I said oh man, they don’t like my music, wow. So anyway, next recess I go down to the studio and I said, “Man, what happened?” Well we had a little problem with your chart.” So when I looked at the chart, I don’t know what I was thinking, the first page, the trumpet part was on line 3, next page it was on line 4. I said, oh, we have a little problem over here. So we spent the time rehearsing and getting all the music together. We got it together. That day for every cue going to a commercial they played my song. I was like wow. It was great. Plus I was getting paid.
